## LegatorOCR 0.2.0-pre.71 — adversarial audit

This release is the result of an audit with hostile inputs. Everything found was repaired and each repair has a test that failed before the change.

### Repaired
- **EPUB / TEI / XLSX**: control characters and U+FFFE/U+FFFF from an OCR engine or a hostile text layer no longer make the exported file unreadable for XML parsers.
- **Memory cap**: page size arithmetic saturates instead of overflowing (release builds check overflow).
- **Signing**: temporary directories are created with mode 0700.
- **Time-stamp authority**: only `http://` and `https://` addresses reach curl, after `--proto` and `--`; a value such as `-o…` or `file://…` is refused.
- **External programs** (pdftoppm, veraPDF): a file name starting with `-` is no longer read as an option.

### New
- `scripts/hostile.py` and the `hostile` workflow: corrupt PNG/JPEG/PDF/ZIP inputs, decompression bombs and thousands of pages, run against the CLI under memory and time limits; a panic, hang or unbounded memory fails the build.
- Fuzzing of 137 value-taking CLI options with 12 hostile values each (1,644 runs): no crash, no command injection.

### Known and documented
- Extreme inputs (400 MP image, 3,000-page PDF) are slow but bounded; see docs/ADVERSARIAL-ANALYSIS.md.

Built and tested by the CI of this release.
